subject: ventures/route-account-pruner
professional: a route-service / route-distribution operations manager (lawn, pool, pest or delivery routes) who runs cost-to-serve reviews and prunes or reprices unprofitable stops; first checks: is cost to serve per stop (on-site + drive time, vehicle, materials, crew labour) computed right, does dropping a stop really free the time and is that time refillable, is the recommended raise a sensible number (break-even plus margin under a stated elasticity), and do the verdicts survive a different hour value

evidence.correctness: Recomputed outside the author's code with my own Python (scratchpad rap/indep.py: closed-form economics and the analytic optimum of (1 - k x)(s + M x), x* = (1/k + a)/2, a = -s/M, rounded to the 1% grid; the sample's LCG re-implemented in Python). The page's own placeholder rows: Smith 160/4/45/8/12 -> hours 3.5333, net 141.60, yield 40.0755, surplus -88.0667, drop; Oak St Duplex 120/4/30/35/10 -> 4.3333, 82.00, 18.9231, -199.6667, drop: tool identical (node -e on calc.mjs). Sample book of 40 at defaults: surplus now 197.47, plan 1,476.62, gain 1,279.15, 185.87 route hours, $13,480 billed, drive share 20.59%, 10 reprice / 5 drop: tool identical. Interior optimum (M 200, s -10, churn 40% per 10%): my x* 15%, expected 8.00, cancel 60%: tool identical. Sensitivity at $52/$65/$78: keep/reprice/drop 33/7/0, 25/10/5, 7/21/12: tool identical. Wrong outputs on reachable input: a header 'Minutes driving' or 'Driving minutes' (no 'drive' substring) silently swaps drive and on-site minutes (Smith read as onsite 8, drive 45); a 'Price per visit' header with the select left on 'per month' is read as a monthly price with no warning.
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked end to end via node on calc.mjs and reading index.html's script: header reordering by name (works except 'driving'), $/comma/parentheses money parsing, tab/semicolon delimiters, materials optional, per-visit billing (x visits), skipped-row warning, <5 accounts and zero hour value refused, drive >40% and zero-drive warnings, every-account-clears warning, keep/reprice/drop with ties to keep, 100% cancellation treated as drop, sensitivity table, ranking CSV download (41 lines for 40 accounts), opt-out button, related-tool links. No stubs or TODOs. Served copy clean (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs route-account-pruner: 'no placeholder or retired origin left').
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 29 pass, 0 fail, 84 ms (bare `node --test` as the README says also runs 29). Six mutants via quality_mutate.py: caught 2 (cancel-rate scale inc/0.1 -> inc/0.2; driveHours from onsite), survived 4: the repriced surplus 'e.surplus + e.monthly * inc' -> '+ e.net * inc' (core reprice arithmetic), neededIncrease '/ e.monthly' -> '/ e.net' (shown on every reprice/drop row), drive '>= 0' -> '> 0' in parseRows, driveShare warning 0.4 -> 0.6. No test pins a repriced account's increase or expected surplus to a hand number; the reprice test only asserts increase > 0 and expected > surplus.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (174 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs, all three test files. Pure, small, no dependencies, clear comments, errors returned not thrown. Defects: header picker regex /drive|travel|.../ misses 'driving', and the fallback index (calc.mjs:49) is used even when another column already claimed it, so one unmatched header can read the wrong column without a warning; reportCsv strips commas but neither quotes fields nor escapes leading = + - @ (a name '=cmd|x' is written as-is, CSV formula injection when opened in Excel); 'increase: k / 100' duplicates STEP.
evidence.claims: Backed: no upload (page.test bans fetch/XHR/beacon in index, calc and usage; usage.mjs is localStorage only and honours DNT/GPC), disclaimer and no-warranty on page and README, 'Unverified' and 'Not modelled' lists present, cancellation rate labelled an assumption, formulas on the page match calc.mjs, served llms.txt/sitemap clean. Not backed as worded: the headline tile 'Expected gain a month if you make them' (sample: +$1,279) counts each freed route hour at the hour value; in cash, the 5 dropped sample accounts lose $1,305.80 a month of net income and free 27.8 hours that only pay back if refilled at $65. The tile carries no such caveat; a reader acting on 'gain' drops customers.
evidence.fitness: Job: an owner of a 1-5 crew lawn/pool route deciding which accounts to raise or cut before the season. Pasting an export and getting a worst-first ranking with drive share and hour-value sensitivity is genuinely useful as a first screen. Gaps hit in the first hour: crew size and paid labour are not separate from the hour value (a 2-person crew's on-site hour is two wages); every recommended raise under the default churn equals the cap (all 10 in the sample at 25%), so the 'best increase' is the user's limit, not an analysis; every negative-surplus account that cannot be repriced is dropped, which is right only if freed hours refill; an export with 'Minutes driving' headers silently produces wrong ranks.
evidence.domain: Matches practice: activity-based cost to serve per stop (time on site + marginal drive time, vehicle cost on drive hours, direct materials) compared with an opportunity value of route time, and a sensitivity check, as in route-distribution cost-to-serve reviews. Departs: no crew-size multiplier or loaded labour rate separate from opportunity value; linear cancellation with the default 1:1 elasticity makes (1-x)(s+Mx) peak at x >= 50%, so the grid search always lands on the cap and the page does not flag the corner; drop is valued as if freed hours refill at the hour value at once (replacement cost is in 'Not modelled' but not reflected in the headline gain); marginal drive time is asked for but drop of a stop in a dense cluster is not distinguished from an outlying one (stated limit).

defects.what: Header picker's drive regex /drive|travel|transit|commute/ misses 'driving'; with headers 'Driving minutes' / 'Minutes driving' the fallback index (calc.mjs:49, not checked against used columns) and the onsite regex's 'minutes' swap on-site and drive minutes silently (Smith read as 8 on site, 45 driving), so ranks and drive share are wrong.

Headline tile 'Expected gain a month if you make them' (+$1,279 on the sample) values every freed route hour at the hour value; in cash the 5 drops lose $1,305.80/mo of net income and free 27.8 h that pay only if refilled. No caveat on the tile.

With the default linear 1:1 cancellation response, (1-x)(s+Mx) peaks at x >= 50%, so every recommended raise is exactly the user's cap (all 10 sample reprices at 25%); the page calls it the best increase and never says the limit, not the analysis, picked it.

Core reprice arithmetic and the break-even increase shown on every row are untested: mutants 'e.monthly * inc' -> 'e.net * inc' (calc.mjs:94) and '-e.surplus / e.monthly' -> '/ e.net' (calc.mjs:104) leave all 29 tests green; no test pins a repriced account's increase/expected to a hand number.
A 'Price per visit' header with the 'Price column is' select left on per month is read as a monthly price with no warning (40/visit x 4 becomes $40/month), pushing the account to drop.

Crew size and paid labour are not modelled separately from the hour value: a route hour is a truck hour, so a two-person crew's on-site time costs two wages and the surplus of long on-site accounts is overstated.
Boundaries untested: zero drive minutes accepted by parseRows (mutant '>= 0' -> '> 0' survives) and the 40% drive-share warning threshold (0.4 -> 0.6 survives).
reportCsv writes names unquoted (commas stripped) with no escape for a leading = + - @, so a customer name like '=cmd|x' is a live formula when the download is opened in Excel (CSV injection).

verdict: The arithmetic is right where I recomputed it independently: my Python closed form reproduces the page's placeholder rows, the 40-account sample's totals (surplus 197.47 -> 1,476.62, 10 reprice / 5 drop, 20.59% driving), an interior reprice optimum from calculus (15%, expected 8.00) and the sensitivity counts exactly. It does not meet the bar: 4 of 6 seeded mutants survive, including the repriced-surplus formula and the break-even increase shown on every row (verification 2); the headline 'Expected gain a month' counts freed hours as refilled at the hour value, so the sample's +$1,279 'gain' is a $1,306 monthly cash loss until those 27.8 hours are resold, with no caveat on the tile (claims 2). A route operations manager would also notice that under the default cancellation assumption every raise is exactly the cap, that crew size is absent, and that an export headed 'Minutes driving' silently swaps drive and on-site time. A good first screen, not yet a pruning decision tool.
